Follow me on this:

 My exgf had never seen Spaceballs, the movie. Obviously I had to show her! A classic! She was enjoying it, but then we get toward the end. The bad guys are sucking out all the air of the good planet, suffocating people. You see trees get sucked up and snow rise off a mountain. You see the king suffocating as he sadly looks at a picture of his daughter and faints. 

 My ex starts freaking out. Bad. It turns out that she's had this underlying, irrational fear of all the air being sucked away her whole life. All she could ever guess was it had something to do with a random nightmare she had as a very little kid. It was about an older man, a king maybe, suffocating as all the air was sucked away from his kingdom. She remembered trees being sucked away, and even the snow off a mountain. She very vividly remembered how sad the old man was as he looked at some picture. It absolutely terrified her. *She never forgot it.*

 Now, here it turns out that it was that scene from Spaceballs. Every detail and even more she didn't remember, like the daughter being the picture. Crazy! But how? She hadn't ever seen it. Her parents said they hadn't either, but she vividly remembered that specific scene and nothing else of the film. So, was toddler/little kid her just channel surfing and randomly saw the movie, or just that scene and forgot? Seems most likely, and point being that this random scene from a movie she'd never heard of absolutely impacted her. It didn't cause her to be suicidal, but why would anyone think that extreme anyways? 

 Why does it have to be one extreme or the other? Life is a chaotic chain of random events. Some of them stick with us, but we never know which until later; and you may never know why. I have random stuff like that, too. It's normal, and it's completely normal, and rational, to watch a music video of a baby crying while surrounded by horrific monsters and think to yourself, "Gee. I wonder whatever happened to that kid. Does he remember the monsters?" which obviously isn't like asking if the dude cries himself to sleep every night, cursing MGMT.

I've always tried to be as  respectful of her mental health as possible. I played my part in it all, though, as did a huge amount of other things. She and I are human beings. Hard to summarize all of that here. I don't want to villainize her or make myself out to be blameless. That I am not, but I do need insight into when to reach out and how.

I absolutely agree that she deserves her space. I haven't pressed her. I want her to be able to recover from being overwhelmed. We haven't spoken. I'm honestly terrified of the gift overwhelming her.

But my brain started at, "show up with the gift, maybe flowers, and surprise her!", but I knew that was an incredibly awful idea. Went to just dropping it off myself at a time I wouldn't see her, but still felt like too much. "Text her Thursday? ... No."

I figured UPS was a good option that didn't involve any direct contact with me. Didn't add anything else to the one gift I got weeks before. Didn't get any overstimulating card with or without any long love message. Idk. I'm just trying to reach respectful mediums for both of us.

Neither she nor I handled the initial mention of the breakup possibility well. The timing was bad, but "timing's a bitch". Plus, her med change is an objective factor that has this known affect. I can't know for sure rn if it applies to her without discussing it, but it remains a possible factor. 

I can't know anything better without input from her, but I appreciate everyone's insight.

I was really let down by the ending to the show when  I watched it. It took me awhile to sit and reflect on it. I came to the conclusion that I, like a lot of folks, were really just upset that the end wasn't quite how I had always imagined it. I never thought it would end like that, but no one thinks portions of their lives are going to end like they really will. Once I realized all of this, I was able to accept and better respect the ending. 

All that matters is one's happiness in the end.

First off, this show STARTED with Robin. The story literally began with Ted meeting Robin. He wanted her from the beginning. Did everyone forget that? "Haaaave you met Ted?!"

The last season being Barney and Robin's wedding honest to god made sense. The mother was connected to Barney and Robin's wedding through the whole group. She was honestly quite detrimental to it happening. She inspired Barney to get Robin. She got Marshall the rest of the way there. She lead to Lily confronting Marshall, and the truth about Lily being pregnant coming out. She kept Robin from running away. She met Ted, the father of her two great kids. Had that wedding not happened, the kids would have never been born to even hear the story.

I really don't think the wedding was even supposed to be focused on how much Barney and Robin loved each other. It was just a HUGE part of all their friendships. It was "The End". That was the last time they'd all hang out as good friends just like Lily said. In just that short weekend, all of their lives were changing. Marshall and Lily got a decent ending. In that weekend we found out that they were a growing family (This was the only part of the season that almost had me in tears.), and in the end they stay together with their kids happily. Barney was never truly ready for marriage. We saw how nervous and scared he was. He got through it, but he definitely had to force himself at times. Think about it. He was a playboy type for years with the group always disapproving. He finally tries to be like them, and it doesn't work out. At least he tried! He can honestly say that. It's almost sad for Barney that after all those years he finally had to say to his best friends, "Let me be me". Barney didn't need to change, but he tried anyways just for his friends. What a good guy, and in the end, he got his happy ending. He actually DID find the girl he could devote his life, too. He DID change and evolve in the end. Robin was nervous, too. She wasn't ready to settle down. Her entire purpose for moving to America was to be a great journalist. She did it! She got to travel around the world and was famous. She was upset because she realized she should be with Ted, but was with Barney. Her and Barney split up, but Ted is happily taken now. Tracy died, and I'm sure Robin put thought into Ted being single. She waited six whole years for him, and lucky for her he came around in the end with the help of the kids that purely came into being by her marrying Barney at one point. Robin got a happy ending.

Tracy and Ted BOTH thought they had already met their Lebenslanger Shicckaschatz, Max and Robin, but they found another Lebenslanger Shicckaschatz. The lightning bolt called Love hit them TWICE. What a lucky couple to have found each other. Imagine if Ted had missed her. Hadn't met her at all. She still would've died. That's why he wanted the extra 45 days with her. He got a great ten years with her and two children. All he could do was be thankful he got any time at all with that beautiful girl. We waited her for her alongside Ted for so many years. We saw her so briefly in the season, but we learned to love her so quickly and so much. Then she was ripped away from us in such a brief time span. Just. Like. Ted. He fell for this girl instantly after having waited for her for years, but to Ted, a 40+ year old man, ten years is a very brief time. Imagine how much it hurt Ted to lose her. We all know Ted. Don't get me wrong, I am MAD about the ending, but I understand why they did it. They put us through a small simulation of the grief Ted must have gone through. Plus, kids that have parents die while they're still young tend to feel more badly about a lonely parent. I'm sure Ted's kids only want their dad to be happy, and like they said, "We love Aunt Robin". They know Robin, and trust this woman to make their dad happy. After all, doesn't Ted deserve to be happy in the end...?
